I've finished reading the whole prototype and compared it against the codebase. The two documentation agents (Gemini Live and ElevenLabs) are still running; I'll fold their findings in when they report back. Here's the design review now.

## What's new in the prototype (multilingual / JA failover)

The current codebase ([lib/data.ts](lib/data.ts)) has no language fields at all, so everything below is new surface to port:

**Data model** (`screens.jsx`)
- Every persona now carries a `ja` alternate block — localized `name` (katakana), `accent` (`JPN · F/M`), `aspect`, `traits`, `desc`, and a `rate` in **mora/min replacing wpm** (e.g. ARIA → アリア, 380 mora/min). `resolvePersona(p, lang)` merges the JA block over the base and stamps `lang` + `rateLabel` so CallView/Sidebar know which voice is armed.
- Providers gain a `ja: true` flag on exactly the four you named — XAI, OPENAI, ELEVENLABS, GOOGLE. Cascade (MISTRAL), FAL.AI, and KYUTAI stay EN-only.

**Personas section**
- Each card gets a compact `EN / 日本語` segmented switch (top-right, `stopPropagation` so flipping language doesn't steal the select-click). Mobile uses `EN / JA` labels.
- JA mode renders the katakana name with the romaji as a small sub-label, JA traits/desc in dedicated Japanese fonts (Zen Kaku Gothic New for UI text, Shippori Mincho for the serif description — mirroring the Plex Mono/Newsreader split), and a `JA VOICE` support line listing the capable vendors.
- If the **armed** persona is JA on a non-JA transport, the card shows a dashed accent warning: `▲ ACTIVE TRANSPORT MISTRAL — NO JA · FAILOVER → OPENAI`.

**Auto-failover** (`app.jsx`, duplicated in Desktop and Mobile shells)
- A `useEffect` watches `(persona, provider)`: when `persona.lang === 'ja' && !provider.ja`, it reroutes to **OPENAI** without dropping the session — call state dips to `CONNECTING` for 1.6s, then resumes `LISTENING`. A `failover` object drives a status strip in CallView: `▲ JA VOICE UNSUPPORTED ON <from> — REROUTING TRANSPORT → <to>`, flipping to `● TRANSPORT REROUTED → <to> · SESSION RESUMED` and clearing after 5.6s. A `failRef` guard prevents re-entry.
- CallView's meta row adds `PERSONA · <name> · JA` and an accent `NO JA ON <provider> · FAILOVER` tag; Providers table adds a small `JA` mark next to capable vendors and an `AUTO-FAILOVER ON` tag in the header.
- `index.html` adds the two Japanese Google-font families.

**Design observations worth carrying into implementation**
1. **Hard-coded failover target.** Both shells do `PROVIDERS.find(x => x.id === 'openai')`. Since four providers support JA, the app version should pick the *best available* JA provider (or the previous JA provider the user used), not literally OpenAI — e.g. first `ja` provider in roster order excluding the current one.
2. **Duplicated effect.** The identical failover effect lives in both `DesktopApp` and `MobileApp`; in the codebase this belongs once in the `SessionApi` layer (a reroute is a transport concern, not a view concern) — especially since real engines mount unconditionally and a mid-call provider swap means tearing down one hook's session and starting another.
3. **The mock "session stays up" is aspirational.** In the real app a provider switch mid-call is a new WebSocket/WebRTC session; transcript continuity is ours to preserve (keep `turns` across the swap), but the agent's conversational context won't carry unless we replay it into the new session's instructions.
4. **The Personas warning renders only for the armed persona** (`on && ja && !provider.ja`), which is correct — but since failover auto-fires ~immediately, the warn state is essentially transient. Worth keeping: it's visible in the moment before/while the strip shows.

★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────
- The design encodes JA capability as a *provider* flag but language as *persona* state — failover is the reconciliation between the two. That's the right split for the codebase too: `Persona.lang` is UI state, `Provider.ja` is static capability data, and the reroute rule lives where both meet (the session layer).
- Switching wpm → mora/min isn't cosmetic: mora rate is the standard Japanese speech-rate unit, and it signals the JA block is a genuine localization, not a translation overlay.
─────────────────────────────────────────────────

**OpenAI** (from your notes, consistent with what I know): `gpt-realtime-2.1` does Japanese speech-to-speech with no `language` parameter — the JA persona's instructions must pin the response language (「常に日本語で応答してください」), while the configured voice stays the same. That maps cleanly onto [openai-agent.ts](lib/realtime/openai-agent.ts)'s per-persona `instructions`: a JA persona variant just needs a JA instruction block.

I'll report the Gemini Live and ElevenLabs documentation findings (exact config fields for language, voices, and per-session overrides) as soon as the two research agents complete.

## 1. Japanese conversations: yes, fully supported

Japanese (`ja`) is a first-class agent language. Config knobs:

- **Agent language**: `conversation_config.agent.language: "ja"` (ISO 639-1; default `"en"`).
- **TTS model** (`conversation_config.tts.model_id`) — Japanese-capable options for agents:
  - `eleven_flash_v2_5` — 32 languages incl. `ja`, ~75 ms, the recommended realtime choice. Note: a new agent defaults to English + Flash **v2** (English-only); adding non-English languages switches it to the v2.5 multilingual model automatically.
  - `eleven_turbo_v2_5` — supports `ja` but is now **deprecated**; docs say use `eleven_flash_v2_5` instead (functionally equivalent, lower latency).
  - `eleven_multilingual_v2` — 29 languages incl. `ja`, higher quality, higher latency.
  - `eleven_v3_conversational` — 70+ languages incl. Japanese (`jpn`); the agents-flavored v3. Related: "Expressive mode" (`tts.expressive_mode: true`) docs explicitly call out improved expressiveness in Japanese (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/voice/expressive-mode).
- **LLM**: any catalog model (`gemini-2.5-flash`, `gpt-4o`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, etc.) — all mainstream models handle Japanese; no JA-specific LLM setting. Prompting the system prompt in/for Japanese is advisable.
- **ASR**: platform-managed (Scribe; `asr.provider` = `elevenlabs` or `scribe_realtime`), 90+ languages incl. Japanese with automatic language recognition — no per-language ASR config needed.

## 2. Language configuration on the agent

Three layers (docs: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/voice/customization/language):

- **Primary**: `conversation_config.agent.language` (e.g. `"ja"`).
- **Additional languages / presets**: `conversation_config.language_presets` — map of lang code → per-language overrides (first message, voice, etc.):
  ```json
  "language_presets": {
    "ja": {
      "overrides": {
        "agent": { "first_message": "こんにちは。今日はどんなご用件ですか？" },
        "tts": { "voice_id": "<ja-optimized-voice>" }
      }
    }
  }
  ```
  Adding additional languages in the dashboard ("Additional Languages" on the Agent tab) auto-translates the first message via LLM and switches TTS to the v2.5 multilingual model. Presets can also carry `first_message_translation`.
- **Per-session client override**: yes — the conversation-initiation payload accepts `conversation_config_override.agent.language` (docs: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/personalization/overrides). Language selection is **fixed for the call duration** unless the language-detection tool is enabled (see 5).

## 3. React SDK per-session language override

Yes. In `@elevenlabs/react`, overrides are passed as an **option to `useConversation` / `ConversationProvider`** (not as a `startSession` argument — `startSession` takes `agentId`/`signedUrl`/`conversationToken`, `userId`, `connectionType`):

```ts
const conversation = useConversation({
  overrides: {
    agent: { language: "ja", firstMessage: "...", prompt: { prompt: "..." } },
    tts: { voiceId: "..." },
  },
});
await conversation.startSession({ agentId });
```

(Docs: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/libraries/react — "Conversation overrides" section. In Tsubaki's vendored setup, pass `overrides` at the `ConversationProvider` level since provider props mirror hook options.)

**Required agent-side enablement** — overrides are disabled by default for security; enable per-field on the agent's **Security** tab, or via API:

```json
"platform_settings": {
  "overrides": {
    "conversation_config_override": {
      "agent": { "language": true, "first_message": true, "prompt": { "prompt": true } },
      "tts": { "voice_id": true }
    }
  }
}
```

Sending an override for a field not enabled here throws an error (except ASR keywords, which soft-fail). Omit fields you don't override — don't send null/empty.

## 4. Japanese voices

- Japanese is covered by all multilingual TTS models (`eleven_flash_v2_5`, `eleven_multilingual_v2`, `eleven_v3`/`eleven_v3_conversational`; `eleven_turbo_v2_5` deprecated). Models page: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models.
- Any voice can technically speak `ja` through a multilingual model, but docs recommend a **language-specific voice** for natural pronunciation/accent. No specific voice IDs are named in docs; curated picks live at the Voice Library "language top picks" collections: https://elevenlabs.io/app/voice-library/collections (filter Japanese). The skill's "popular voices" (George, Sarah, etc.) are English-oriented defaults — audition a JA-native voice instead (and per project memory, the user auditions persona voices by ear).
- Set the JA voice either as the agent's main `tts.voice_id` (single-language JA agent) or in `language_presets.ja.overrides.tts.voice_id` (multilingual agent).

## 5. Auto language detection: yes

The `language_detection` **system tool** (https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/tools/system-tools/language-detection):

- Not enabled by default. Enable via dashboard (Add tool → system) or API as a tool under `conversation_config.agent.prompt.tools`:
  ```json
  { "type": "system", "name": "language_detection", "description": "" }
  ```
  (Also appears as `built_in_tools.language_detection` in the skill's built-in tools table; the docs' API example uses the `tools` array form with `"type": "system"`.)
- Triggers on (a) user speaking a different language than current output, (b) user explicitly asking to switch. Tool params: `reason`, `language` (must be in the agent's configured language list).
- Target languages must be configured as additional languages (`language_presets`) — docs recommend enabling all languages + the tool for multilingual agents. Switching swaps voice + responses per the presets.
- Without this tool, language is fixed for the whole call.

# Gemini Live API — Japanese support for realtime speech-to-speech

## 1. Does the Live API support Japanese speech in/out? Which models?

**Yes.** Japanese (`ja`) is on the official Live API supported-languages list (70 languages) for both speech input and audio output.

- **Current model: `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview`** (native audio output; the model this project already uses in `/Users/jessearmand/Develop/realtime-persona/lib/realtime/gemini-agent.ts`) — full Japanese in/out.
- `gemini-2.5-flash-native-audio-preview-12-2025` (native audio) — supported Japanese, but is **deprecated**; migrate to 3.1.
- **Half-cascade models (`gemini-live-2.5-flash-preview`, `gemini-2.0-flash-live-001`) are already shut down** (shutdown date was December 9, 2025). As of today there is no half-cascade option — every live model is native-audio.
- `gemini-3.5-live-translate-preview` exists separately for live streaming translation (70+ languages).

Source: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/live-guide (Supported languages table; Japanese = `ja`).

## 2. Language configuration — `languageCode` in `speechConfig`

The field exists in the API schema but **native-audio models do not support it**. Verbatim from the capabilities guide:

> "Native audio output models automatically choose the appropriate language and **don't support explicitly setting the language code**."

So for `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` you do **not** set a language — the model auto-detects from spoken input, and you steer it via system instructions (see #5).

For completeness, the schema shape (this was only honored by the now-retired half-cascade models; sending it to a native-audio model is at best ignored):

`SpeechConfig` (defined at https://ai.google.dev/api/generate-content#SpeechConfig, referenced by the Live setup's `generationConfig`):

```json
{
  "voiceConfig": { "prebuiltVoiceConfig": { "voiceName": string } },
  "multiSpeakerVoiceConfig": { ... },   // mutually exclusive with voiceConfig
  "languageCode": string                 // BCP-47; ja-JP is a valid value
}
```

Documented valid `languageCode` values include **`ja-JP`** (full list: `de-DE, en-AU, en-GB, en-IN, en-US, es-US, fr-FR, hi-IN, pt-BR, ar-XA, es-ES, fr-CA, id-ID, it-IT, ja-JP, tr-TR, vi-VN, bn-IN, gu-IN, kn-IN, ml-IN, mr-IN, ta-IN, te-IN, nl-NL, ko-KR, cmn-CN, pl-PL, ru-RU, th-TH`).

**Exact WebSocket setup-message shape** (first and only first client message; same for the `BidiGenerateContentConstrained` endpoint — setup goes inside `generationConfig`):

```json
{
  "setup": {
    "model": "models/gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview",
    "generationConfig": {
      "responseModalities": ["AUDIO"],
      "speechConfig": {
        "voiceConfig": { "prebuiltVoiceConfig": { "voiceName": "Kore" } }
        // "languageCode": "ja-JP"  <- schema-valid but NOT supported by native-audio models
      }
    },
    "systemInstruction": { "parts": [{ "text": "..." }] },
    "inputAudioTranscription": {},
    "outputAudioTranscription": {}
  }
}
```

## Provider-by-provider: how Japanese actually gets configured

**Gemini Live** — nothing to configure. `gemini-3.1-flash-live-preview` (the model [gemini-agent.ts](lib/realtime/gemini-agent.ts) already targets) supports Japanese in/out natively; `ja` is on the official 70-language list. Two important caveats:
- **Do not send `speechConfig.languageCode`** — the field exists in the schema (`ja-JP`) but native-audio models explicitly don't support it; only the now-shut-down half-cascade models honored it. Native audio auto-detects the spoken language.
- To **force** Japanese responses, the only supported control is the system instruction (e.g. 「常に日本語で応答してください」) in the persona prompt. Voices are language-agnostic — every prebuilt voice (Puck, Kore, Charon, …) speaks Japanese, so the existing per-persona voice casting carries over unchanged. Transcripts (input/output) come back in Japanese automatically; `inputAudioTranscription`/`outputAudioTranscription` have no language knob.

**OpenAI** — same pattern as Gemini, per your notes: `gpt-realtime-2.1` has no `language` setting; JA is instruction-driven, voice unchanged. Worth testing pronunciation of names/numbers/honorifics with real Japanese audio before trusting it.

**ElevenLabs** — the only provider where JA is a *config* concern, on three levels:
1. Agent: `conversation_config.agent.language: "ja"`, TTS model `eleven_flash_v2_5` (turbo v2.5 is deprecated; v3-conversational also covers JA). Adding a non-English language auto-switches a new agent off the English-only Flash v2.
2. Multilingual agent: `language_presets.ja` carries the JA first message and a JA-optimized `voice_id` — docs recommend a JA-native voice over pushing an English voice through the multilingual model (fits your audition-by-ear casting).
3. Per-session from our client: `useConversation({ overrides: { agent: { language: "ja" } } })` — passed at the hook/provider level, **not** `startSession` — and it hard-fails unless the override is enabled on the agent's **Security tab** (`platform_settings.overrides.conversation_config_override.agent.language: true`). There's also an optional `language_detection` system tool for mid-call auto-switching; without it, language is fixed for the call.

**xAI Grok** — per-persona model/voice/prompt already live in [xai-agent.ts](lib/realtime/xai-agent.ts); JA would follow the same instruction-driven pattern as OpenAI (no doc'd language field in the WS protocol we use).

The design's premise holds: XAI / OPENAI / ELEVENLABS / GOOGLE as `ja: true`, cascade + PersonaPlex as EN-only failover sources. Implementation notes beyond the design-review points I gave earlier:

Failover target.** With a dedicated JA agent (`f7d7lAUw08B7Qx2bCHlP`, JA-native cloned voice), ElevenLabs becomes the *quality* pick, and the whole security-tab override dance from my earlier research becomes unnecessary — arming JA on ElevenLabs is just connecting to the JA agent ID instead of the EN one, no `overrides.agent.language`, no `language_presets`. **2 & 3. Transition, not mid-call reroute.** Agreed — the honest UX is: end the current session, show the failover strip, start a fresh session on the new provider, and carry the transcript `turns` across the swap in UI state. The design's `CONNECTING` dip actually depicts this fine; only the copy "SESSION RESUMED" oversells it — "NEW SESSION · <provider>" would be truthful.

**4. Reverse direction: persona yields to provider.** This is the important refinement over the prototype. The design has one symmetric effect watching `(persona, provider)` that always reroutes the provider — with your rule, the two directions do opposite things, so the trigger must be *which side the user changed*, not the combined state (otherwise the two rules fight each other in a loop):

- User arms a **JA persona** → provider yields: reroute to previous-JA / ElevenLabs.

# ElevenLabs Agents Platform

Build voice AI agents with natural conversations, multiple LLM providers, custom tools, and easy web embedding.

> **Setup:** See [Installation Guide](references/installation.md) for CLI and SDK setup.

## Quick Start with CLI

The ElevenLabs CLI is the recommended way to create and manage agents:

```bash
# Install CLI and authenticate
npm install -g @elevenlabs/cli
elevenlabs auth login

# Initialize project and create an agent
elevenlabs agents init
elevenlabs agents add "My Assistant" --template complete

# Push to ElevenLabs platform
elevenlabs agents push
```

**Available templates:** `complete`, `minimal`, `voice-only`, `text-only`, `customer-service`, `assistant`

### Python

```python
from elevenlabs import ElevenLabs

client = ElevenLabs()

agent = client.conversational_ai.agents.create(
    name="My Assistant",
    conversation_config={
        "agent": {
            "first_message": "Hello! How can I help?",
            "language": "en",
            "prompt": {
                "prompt": "You are a helpful assistant. Be concise and friendly.",
                "llm": "gemini-2.0-flash",
                "temperature": 0.7
            }
        },
        "tts": {"voice_id": "JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb"}
    }
)
```

### JavaScript

```javascript
import { ElevenLabsClient } from "@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js";
const client = new ElevenLabsClient();

const agent = await client.conversationalAi.agents.create({
  name: "My Assistant",
  conversationConfig: {
    agent: {
      firstMessage: "Hello! How can I help?",
      language: "en",
      prompt: {
        prompt: "You are a helpful assistant.",
        llm: "gemini-2.0-flash",
        temperature: 0.7
      }
    },
    tts: { voiceId: "JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb" }
  }
});
```

### cURL

```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/create" \
  -H "xi-api-key: $ELEVENLABS_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "My Assistant", "conversation_config": {"agent": {"first_message": "Hello!", "language": "en", "prompt": {"prompt": "You are helpful.", "llm": "gemini-2.0-flash"}}, "tts": {"voice_id": "JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb"}}}'
```

## Starting Conversations

### Temporary LiveKit WebSocket Pin

Until the ElevenLabs LiveKit server supports `/rtc/v1`, browser clients using WebRTC can fail or stall during the underlying LiveKit WebSocket handshake with `livekit-client` versions newer than `2.16.1`. For React, Next.js, Electron, or other `@elevenlabs/client` / `@elevenlabs/react` integrations that use `connectionType: "webrtc"` or hit `wss://livekit.rtc.elevenlabs.io/rtc/v1`, add this temporary pin to `package.json`:

```json
{
  "overrides": {
    "livekit-client": "2.16.1"
  }
}
```

Use the pin when the app logs `/rtc/v1` 404s, `v1 RTC path not found`, or `could not establish pc connection` during session startup. This is a LiveKit server compatibility workaround for WebRTC sessions, not the ElevenLabs `connectionType: "websocket"` transport. Remove it after the upstream LiveKit server or SDK issue is fixed.

**Authenticated WebRTC:** Request a session token from your backend. The response includes both
the token and the conversation ID:
```python
session = client.conversational_ai.conversations.get_webrtc_token(
    agent_id="your-agent-id",
)
print(session.token, session.conversation_id)
```

**Server-side (Python):** Get signed URL for client connection:
```python
signed_url = client.conversational_ai.conversations.get_signed_url(
    agent_id="your-agent-id",
    environment="staging",
)
```

**Client-side (JavaScript):**
```javascript
import { Conversation } from "@elevenlabs/client";

const conversation = await Conversation.startSession({
  agentId: "your-agent-id",
  environment: "staging",
  overrides: { asr: { keywords: ["ElevenLabs", "TechCorp"] } },
  onMessage: (msg) => console.log("Agent:", msg.message),
  onUserTranscript: (t) => console.log("User:", t.message),
  onPing: (event) => console.log("Estimated latency:", event.ping_ms),
  onError: (e) => console.error(e)
});
```

**React Hook:** Wrap hook consumers in `ConversationProvider`. Prefer granular hooks such as
`useConversationControls` and `useConversationStatus` for session controls and UI state;
`useConversation` remains available as the convenience all-in-one hook. Pass provider-level
callbacks such as `onError` when you want React to handle conversation errors in one place.
```typescript
import {
  ConversationProvider,
  useConversationControls,
  useConversationStatus,
} from "@elevenlabs/react";

function Agent({ signedUrl }: { signedUrl: string }) {
  const { startSession, endSession } = useConversationControls();
  const { status } = useConversationStatus();

  if (status === "connected") {
    return <button onClick={endSession}>End conversation</button>;
  }

  return (
    <button onClick={() => startSession({ signedUrl })}>
      Start conversation
    </button>
  );
}

function App({ signedUrl }: { signedUrl: string }) {
  return (
    <ConversationProvider
      onError={(error) => console.error("Conversation error:", error)}
      onPing={(event) => console.log("Estimated latency:", event.ping_ms)}
    >
      <Agent signedUrl={signedUrl} />
    </ConversationProvider>
  );
}
```

| Anthropic | `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-4-5`, `claude-sonnet-4`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, `claude-3-7-sonnet`, `claude-3-5-sonnet`, `claude-3-haiku` |
| Google | `gemini-3.1-flash-lite-preview`, `gemini-3.1-pro-preview`, `gemini-3-pro-preview`, `gemini-3-flash-preview`, `gemini-2.5-flash`, `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`, `gemini-2.0-flash`, `gemini-2.0-flash-lite` |
| ElevenLabs | `glm-45-air-fp8`, `qwen3-30b-a3b`, `qwen36-35b-a3b`, `qwen35-35b-a3b`, `qwen35-397b-a17b`, `gpt-oss-120b` |
| Custom | `custom-llm` (bring your own endpoint) |

Use `GET /v1/convai/llm/list` to inspect the current model catalog, including deprecation state, token/context limits, capability flags such as image-input support, and model-specific reasoning effort support.

**Popular voices:** `JBFqnCBsd6RMkjVDRZzb` (George), `EXAVITQu4vr4xnSDxMaL` (Sarah), `onwK4e9ZLuTAKqWW03F9` (Daniel), `XB0fDUnXU5powFXDhCwa` (Charlotte)

**Turn eagerness:** `patient` (waits longer for user to finish), `normal`, or `eager` (responds quickly)

See [Agent Configuration](references/agent-configuration.md) for all options.

## System Prompt Structure

Section the prompt with markdown headings — the model prioritizes and interprets instructions more reliably ([prompting guide](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/best-practices/prompting-guide)):

```
# Personality   – named character, 2-3 traits
# Environment   – where they work, who they talk to
# Tone          – vocal style as 4-5 bullets
# Goal          – what success looks like (numbered for multi-step flows)
```

Keep instructions short and action-based. Mark critical steps with "This step is important." For critical refusal/safety rules, include concise instructions in the prompt and also configure independent custom Guardrails via `platform_settings.guardrails` (see [Guardrails](#guardrails)).

## Tools

Extend agents with webhook, client, or built-in system tools. Tools are defined inside `conversation_config.agent.prompt`:

Workspace environment variables can resolve per-environment server tool URLs, headers, and auth connections, and runtime system variables such as `{{system__conversation_history}}` can pass full conversation context into tool calls when needed.

```python
"prompt": {
    "prompt": "You are a helpful assistant that can check the weather.",
    "llm": "gemini-2.0-flash",
    "tools": [
        # Webhook: server-side API call
        {"type": "webhook", "name": "get_weather", "description": "Get weather",
         "api_schema": {"url": "https://api.example.com/weather", "method": "POST",
             "request_body_schema": {"type": "object", "properties": {"location": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["location"]}}},
        # Client: runs in the browser
        {"type": "client", "name": "show_product", "description": "Display a product",
         "parameters": {"type": "object", "properties": {"productId": {"type": "string"}}, "required": ["productId"]}}
    ],
    "built_in_tools": {
        "end_call": {},
        "transfer_to_number": {"transfers": [{"transfer_destination": {"type": "phone", "phone_number": "+1234567890"}, "condition": "User asks for human support"}]},
        "start_procedure": {}
    }
}
```

**Client tools** run in browser:
```javascript
clientTools: {
  show_product: async ({ productId }) => {
    document.getElementById("product").src = `/products/${productId}`;
    return { success: true };
  }
}
```

See [Client Tools Reference](references/client-tools.md) for complete documentation.

### Built-in System Tools

Set under `conversation_config.agent.prompt.built_in_tools`. `{}` enables defaults; provide `description` to customize; omit to disable.

| Tool | Enable for |
|------|------------|
| `end_call` | All agents |
| `language_detection` | Multilingual agents |
| `transfer_to_number` | Phone-based human escalation |
| `transfer_to_agent` | Multi-agent workflows |
| `start_procedure` | Procedure-guided conversations (see [Procedures](#procedures)) |
| `end_procedure` | Completing active procedures |
| `skip_turn` | Tutoring / coaching (silent listening) |
| `voicemail_detection` | Outbound calling |
| `play_keypad_touch_tone` | IVR navigation |

`run_subagent` is a system tool for delegating a task to another configured agent. Add it to
`conversation_config.agent.prompt.tools` with `params.system_tool_type: "run_subagent"` and an
`agents` array. Each entry requires `agent_id` and `description`; `branch_id` and a JSON-schema
`parameters` object are optional.

`knowledge_base` is a system tool for letting the model choose how to inspect attached knowledge.
Add it to `conversation_config.agent.prompt.tools` with `type: "system"`, a `name`, and
`params.system_tool_type: "knowledge_base"`. Use `enabled_strategies` to expose any combination of
`cat`, `keyword`, `semantic`, and `ls`:

```json
{
  "type": "system",
  "name": "knowledge_base",
  "description": "Search the attached knowledge base.",
  "params": {
    "system_tool_type": "knowledge_base",
    "enabled_strategies": ["semantic", "keyword"]
  }
}
```

### Integration Tools

Pre-built connectors managed by the platform. Create a connection with credentials, then attach via `tool_ids`:

| Integration | Use case |
|-------------|----------|
| `calcom` | Scheduling appointments |
| `salesforce` | CRM lookups, case creation |
| `hubspot` | CRM, marketing, contacts |
| `zendesk` | Support ticketing |

Three-step flow: `POST /v1/convai/api-integrations/{id}/connections` → `GET /v1/convai/api-integrations/{id}/tools` → `POST /v1/convai/tools` with `api_integration_id` and `api_integration_connection_id`. Attach to the agent with `"prompt": {"tool_ids": ["tool_xxxx"]}`. Inline `tools` and `tool_ids` can coexist — prefer an integration over a duplicate custom webhook.

### Public-API Webhook Examples

No-auth APIs useful for prototypes (URLs must be HTTPS):

| Tool | URL | Purpose |
|------|-----|---------|
| `get_weather` | `https://wttr.in/{location}?format=j1` | Current weather |
| `search_wikipedia` | `https://en.wikipedia.org/api/rest_v1/page/summary/{topic}` | Topic summary |
| `get_exchange_rate` | `https://open.er-api.com/v6/latest/{base_currency}` | FX rates |

## Workflows

Route conversations through discrete steps with branching logic. Define under the agent's top-level `workflow` field. Reference: [Agent Workflows](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/agent-workflows).

**Node types:** `start` (ID must be `"start_node"`), `end`, `override_agent` (subagent step with `label` + `additional_prompt`), `dispatch_tool` (executes a tool with success/failure routing), `agent_transfer`, `transfer_to_number`.

**Edge types:** `unconditional`, `llm` (natural-language condition), `expression` (deterministic data check). Tool nodes have separate success/failure edges.

**Scope tools per step** with `additional_tool_ids` on a node — prevents the wrong tool firing at the wrong step. Set `additional_tool_ids: []` on conversational routing nodes such as greeting and `classify_intent` so they only converse:

```json
{
  "type": "override_agent",
  "label": "Book Appointment",
  "additional_prompt": "Discuss preferred dates and doctors. Show the booking form once agreed.",
  "entry_behavior": "wait_for_user",
  "additional_tool_ids": ["show_booking_form", "display_appointment_card"],
  "position": {"x": 0, "y": 400}
}
```

Include `position` (`{x, y}`) on every node so the editor renders cleanly. Start at `y=0`, put `end` at the bottom, and space branches horizontally at `x=-150` and `x=150`; suggested spacing is 200px vertical between levels and 300px horizontal between branches. Keep workflows to 4-7 nodes and always have a path to `end`.

Use `entry_behavior` on `override_agent` nodes to choose whether a sub-agent speaks immediately (`generate_immediately`), waits for user input (`wait_for_user`), or lets the platform decide (`auto`).

For nested agent transfers, set `enable_nesting` on a `standalone_agent` node and
`return_when_nested` on an `end` node that should return control to the parent workflow.

## Procedures

Reusable instruction blocks an agent runs when a trigger matches. A procedure is `free_form` (markdown guidance the agent adapts, and the only type that can reference knowledge base documents) or `deterministic` (ordered, typed steps for flows that must run consistently). Procedures are in Alpha. See [Using the Procedure API](references/using-procedure-api.md) for the full REST and SDK flow, and [Writing Procedures](references/writing-procedures.md) for the step schema and authoring rules.

Procedures live on an agent branch, and every write stages a per-user draft:

| Operation | Call |
|-----------|------|
| List, create, read, update, discard, remove | `/v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/branches/{branch_id}/procedures...` (`procedures.*` and `procedures.drafts.*` in the SDKs) |
| Compile | `POST .../procedures/compile` (`procedures.compile`) |
| Publish | `PATCH /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}?branch_id=...` (`agents.update`) |

Semantics worth knowing before writing any of these calls:

- Nothing reaches the live agent until you publish. Publishing is not a procedure endpoint; one PATCH on the agent versions every changed procedure draft on the branch.
- `GET .../procedures/{procedure_id}` reads branch HEAD and returns `404` until that procedure's first publish. Read the `/draft` variant to see a procedure you just created; do not retry the create.
- Compile only when structured (`deterministic`) procedures changed. Compilation turns them into workflow nodes, so the publish must carry the `workflow` that compile returned. Free-form-only changes publish without compiling, because the agent loads free-form procedures from their published versions.
- Compile validates structured content and is the only way to check it. On `400` it returns `errors` keyed by procedure ID with the offending field `path`; repair the draft and compile again rather than publishing.
- A draft update replaces the whole body. Read the draft first, then resend `name`, `type`, and `trigger` alongside the new `content`.
- `content` is markdown for a `free_form` procedure, and a JSON-encoded object with a `trigger` and a `steps` array for a `deterministic` one. Serialize it; do not hand-escape quotes.
- Routing is driven by the `trigger` text, not the procedure name. Write concrete, non-overlapping triggers that cover the phrasings a user would actually say.
- Procedure APIs require `elevenlabs` (Python) or `@elevenlabs/elevenlabs-js` at `2.60.0` or newer.

## Guardrails

Layered safety enforcement that runs independently of the LLM — configured under `platform_settings.guardrails`, not in the system prompt. Reference: [Guardrails](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/best-practices/guardrails).

```json
"platform_settings": {
  "guardrails": {
    "version": "1",
    "focus": {"is_enabled": true},
    "prompt_injection": {"is_enabled": true},
    "content": {"config": {"harassment": {"is_enabled": true, "threshold": 0.5}}},
    "custom": {
      "config": {
        "configs": [{
          "is_enabled": true,
          "name": "No medical diagnoses",
          "prompt": "Block the agent from providing medical diagnoses or treatment advice.",
          "execution_mode": "blocking",
          "model": "gemini-2.5-flash-lite",
          "history_message_count": 1,
          "trigger_action": {"type": "retry", "feedback": "Reason: {{trigger_reason}}"}
        }]
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Types:** `focus` (on-topic), `prompt_injection` (manipulation defense), `content` (category filters), `custom` (LLM-evaluated domain rules). Content categories include `harassment`, `profanity`, `sexual`, `violence`, `self_harm`, and `medical_and_legal_information` — threshold range `0.0`–`1.0` (default `0.3`). Custom rules use `execution_mode: "blocking"` with a `model`, `history_message_count`, and `trigger_action` (e.g., `retry` with feedback). Custom guardrails evaluate in parallel and fail-open.

**Per vertical:** healthcare/finance/legal → enable `medical_and_legal_information`; education/youth → `sexual`/`violence`/`self_harm`/`profanity`; support/sales → `harassment`/`profanity`. All agents benefit from `focus` + `prompt_injection` + 2-4 custom rules.

## Testing Agents

Three test types via `POST /v1/convai/agent-testing/create`, then attached with PATCH on the agent. Reference: [Agent Testing](https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-agents/customization/agent-testing).

| Type | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `llm` | Scenario test — does the agent respond appropriately to a message? |
| `tool` | Tool-call test — right tool, right parameters? |
| `simulation` | Multi-turn flow with a simulated user persona |

```json
// Tool-call test (snake_case throughout; chat_history role is "user" or "agent")
{
  "name": "Books with correct doctor and date",
  "type": "tool",
  "chat_history": [
    {"role": "user", "message": "Dr. Smith on March 5 at 2pm", "time_in_call_secs": 10}
  ],
  "tool_call_parameters": {
    "referenced_tool": {"id": "show_booking_form", "type": "client"},
    "parameters": [
      {"path": "doctor_name", "eval": {"type": "llm", "description": "Should reference Dr. Smith"}},
      {"path": "date", "eval": {"type": "regex", "pattern": "2025-03-05|March 5"}}
    ]
  }
}
```

Eval strategies: `exact`, `regex`, `llm`. Prompt evaluation criteria can use binary scoring or
numeric scoring with `scoring_mode: "numeric_uniform"`, `max_score`, and `score_instructions`;
numeric scores are normalized into the aggregate conversation success percentage. Attach via PATCH:

```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "https://api.elevenlabs.io/v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}" \
  -H "xi-api-key: $ELEVENLABS_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"platform_settings": {"testing": {"attached_tests": [{"test_id": "test_xxxx"}]}}}'
```

Run selected tests with `POST /v1/convai/agents/{agent_id}/run-tests`. The request
body requires `tests` and accepts `repeat_count` from `1` to `50` for repeated runs.
Simulation tests can define up to 30 `success_conditions` prompts; all criteria are
evaluated and merged into the final result.
Simulation tests can also define `tool_mock_overrides`, keyed by tool ID, to replace shared response
mocks for one test. Each override is an array of mocks with a required `mock_result`; set
`is_error: true` to exercise a tool-failure path. Overrides only apply to tools enabled for mocking
through `tool_mock_config`.
For completed conversations, rerun one evaluation criterion with `POST /v1/convai/conversations/{conversation_id}/analysis/evaluations/run` and a request body containing `evaluation_id`.

## Outbound Calls

Make outbound phone calls using your agent via Twilio or Exotel integration:

    call_recording_enabled=True

print(f"Call initiated: {response.conversation_id}")

  agentId: "your-agent-id",
  agentPhoneNumberId: "your-phone-number-id",
  toNumber: "+1234567890",

```bash

  -H "xi-api-key: $ELEVENLABS_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

```

## Managing Agents

### Using CLI (Recommended)

```bash
# List agents and check status
elevenlabs agents list
elevenlabs agents status

# Import agents from platform to local config
elevenlabs agents pull                      # Import all agents
elevenlabs agents pull --agent <agent-id>   # Import specific agent

# Push local changes to platform
elevenlabs agents push              # Upload configurations
elevenlabs agents push --dry-run    # Preview changes first

# Add tools
elevenlabs tools add-webhook "Weather API"
elevenlabs tools add-client "UI Tool"
```

### Project Structure

The CLI creates a project structure for managing agents:

```
your_project/
├── agents.json       # Agent definitions
├── tools.json        # Tool configurations
├── tests.json        # Test configurations
├── agent_configs/    # Individual agent configs
├── tool_configs/     # Individual tool configs
└── test_configs/     # Individual test configs
```

### SDK Examples

```python
# List
agents = client.conversational_ai.agents.list()

# Get
agent = client.conversational_ai.agents.get(agent_id="your-agent-id")

# Update (partial - only include fields to change)
client.conversational_ai.agents.update(agent_id="your-agent-id", name="New Name")
client.conversational_ai.agents.update(agent_id="your-agent-id",
    conversation_config={
        "agent": {"prompt": {"prompt": "New instructions", "llm": "claude-sonnet-4"}}
    })

# Delete
client.conversational_ai.agents.delete(agent_id="your-agent-id")
```

See [Agent Configuration](references/agent-configuration.md) for all configuration options and SDK examples.

`GET /v1/shared-voices` filters the Voice Library directly:

# Prompt Review — Furutsubaki persona stack

## Verdict

This is a strong, unusually disciplined prompt system. The layered design (shared identity → manifestation → transport) is consistently executed across all four engines, the failure boundaries are real boundaries rather than decoration, and per-engine condensation follows each provider's actual constraints rather than copy-paste. Issues below are mostly edge-case coherence and one substantive gap.

## What works well

- **Utility-first invariant is enforced everywhere.** "Give the clear, useful answer first — character colors the answer, never replaces it" appears in all four `SHARED` blocks, backed by "literal precision on names/dates/numbers." This directly implements the doc's core promise.
- **Boundaries are negative constraints, not vibes.** Each persona carries its anti-failure clause verbatim from the doc's Manifestation Boundaries (`never blustering`, `not flirtatious, possessive, dependent`, `atmosphere never replaces the answer`). Negative constraints are what actually prevent archetype collapse.
- **Engine-appropriate structure.** OpenAI gets labeled sections (`# Role & Manifestation`, `# Pacing`, `# Unclear Audio`, `# Variety`) matching the gpt-realtime skeleton; xAI/Gemini get condensed prose per the think-fast guidance; Cascade stays small-LM-safe. This is the doc's "use the provider's most reliable prompt structure" done correctly.
- **Openings are elicited, not scripted.** `firstMessage` as an imperative direction ("Introduce yourself as Onyx in one weighty…") gives per-session variation and demonstrates the aspect in one line — exactly what the propagation procedure asks for.
- **Pacing lives in transport, not just adjectives.** VAD presets are wired per-persona (`VAD_SNAPPY` for sage/nova, `VAD_PATIENT` for cipher/vesper), so "relaxed" isn't only a prose hope.
- **Graceful degradation**: `DEFAULT_PERSONA_AGENT` fallback in all resolvers; unknown IDs don't crash.

## Substantive issues

**1. Echo has no distress protocol (biggest gap).**
Echo is explicitly scoped to "listens for grief, danger, and truths people struggle to say aloud," yet neither her prompt nor any `SHARED` block says what to do when a user expresses self-harm or crisis intent — the prompt only says "notice distress gently." A persona marketed toward difficult thoughts needs one line: acknowledge seriously, encourage human support, stay in character without pretending to be a counselor. The architecture doc shares this gap, so this is a doc-level fix, not just a prompt patch.

**2. "You know nothing of machines" conflicts with tool use and utility rules.**
All condensed `SHARED` blocks go beyond the doc's "gentle amused refusal" to "you know nothing of machines, companies, or devices." Two collisions:
- xAI sessions carry `web_search`; OpenAI sessions attach Firecrawl. "How did you find that?" breaks the fiction immediately, and the model has no coherent answer available.
- The same paragraph demands literal precision on technical topics — but the tree ostensibly knows nothing of devices. Whether the camellia can explain how a phone works is undefined; expect inconsistent behavior at exactly that boundary.

The OpenAI variant's softer phrasing ("If asked whether you are an AI… a gentle, amused refusal is the whole answer") avoids overcommitting; I'd align the condensed versions to it. Refusing the *identity* claim is safe; claiming *ignorance of the concept* invites provable lies.

**3. OpenAI `VAD_PATIENT` is dead weight.**
`VAD_PATIENT` and `VAD_RELAXED` are byte-identical (`eagerness: "low"`, `interrupt_response: false`) — semantic_vad has no silence-duration knob, so "longest silence tolerance" comments are misleading. Harmless at runtime, but a future reader tuning Cipher's pauses will edit a preset that does nothing distinct. Either drop it or add a comment that it's intentionally aliased on this engine.

## Minor observations

- **Triplicated `SHARED`.** xAI, Gemini, and Cascade carry three verbatim-identical condensed blocks. An identity fix must land in four places (plus the doc). Since all three want the same condensation, one shared constant in a neutral module would remove the drift risk — the OpenAI variant is legitimately different and can stay local.
- **Accent-by-prompt on Gemini is optimistic.** Nova/Vesper request a British read; Laomedeia/Despina aren't British voices, and native-audio models honor accent instructions weakly. Expectation gap only; harmless to leave in.
- **Three-way voice sharing on OpenAI.** Nova, Echo, and Vesper all ride `sage`, differentiated purely by prompt. Deliberate and documented; it's the weakest casting of the set — Echo's intimacy depends almost entirely on prose against a neutral-bright voice.
- **Persona-id `echo` vs OpenAI voice `"echo"` (a different, male voice)** is a footgun for future edits; the comments currently save you, but it's one rename away from a silent mis-cast.
- **Unclear-audio handling dropped from Cascade.** Understandable for token economy, but Cascade is the one engine where input corruption is *routine* (real STT mishears, not hypothetical mic noise). One short line ("if a reply seems garbled or random, ask them to repeat") would likely pay for itself; the small-model budget concern cuts the other way here.
- **Doc is slightly stale**: it frames OpenAI as the sole implemented reference with ports pending, but xAI, Gemini, and Cascade all carry the full seven-manifestation roster already. The propagation procedure's step 8 ("record meaningful differences") output isn't visible anywhere.

## Bottom line

Character design: excellent — coherent mythology, enforceable boundaries, utility protected. Prompt engineering: correct per-provider adaptation. Fix order if you touch it: (1) Echo crisis line, (2) soften the machine-ignorance claim to an identity refusal, (3) de-duplicate the condensed `SHARED`, (4) alias-or-delete `VAD_PATIENT` on OpenAI.

`6b2c373` ("harden persona prompts and dedupe shared identity", committed just before your message) already implements the review's entire fix order for the in-app engines: the Echo crisis boundary across all four providers **and** the architecture doc, the machine-ignorance claim replaced with an identity refusal in every SHARED block, the condensed SHARED de-duplicated into [shared-persona-prompt.ts](lib/realtime/shared-persona-prompt.ts) (xAI/Gemini/Cascade import one constant; OpenAI keeps its labeled variant), and OpenAI's dead-weight `VAD_PATIENT` deleted. content.text:
The prototype has moved on since August — language is now a **session property** (`lang` state in each app shell, derived persona via `resolvePersona`), the switch sits in the call meta row and the Personas header, and only ELEVENLABS is flagged `ja` (matching the agent-ID routing we built). The app branch itself still has zero `lang` wiring, so this review is against the prototype as the spec.

## What the switch reaches today

Persona cards (name/aspect/traits/desc/JA greeting/JA agent line), the call meta `PERSONA` tag + `NO JA AGENT` warning, the failover strip, the sidebar foot (`ARIA · 日本語`), and the Providers `LANGUAGE` spec. Everything else stays English regardless of the switch.

## What's missing for a whole-app switch

**1. Two concepts are conflated and need a decision.** The control is labelled `VOICE LANG` — i.e. which agent speaks — but "apply to the whole application" means it's also the *UI locale*. I'd make one switch drive both (simplest, and a Japanese speaker wants both), rename it just `LANG / 言語`, and treat a separate UI-locale override as a later Settings item if ever needed.

**2. No string layer.** Every label is an inline literal, so there's nothing to flip. The prototype needs a `STRINGS = { en, ja }` dictionary and a `t(key)` helper on the app root, and the same in the app (`lib/i18n.ts`). Un-localized surfaces, by screen:

| Surface | Strings still EN-only |
|---|---|
| Top bar / sidebar / mobile tabs | `SESSION · NETWORK · MIC`, `realtime console`, `— SECTIONS`, `SESSIONS/PERSONAS/PROVIDERS/SETTINGS`, `active persona/transport`, `exec`, `● LIVE` |
| Page headers | eyebrows (`001 / VOICE LIBRARY`), titles (`Personas.` etc.), ledes, `+ CLONE NEW`, `IMPORT`, the empty clone-slot copy |
| Call view | state labels `IDLE…ENDED`, placeholder captions (`press CALL to begin`, `establishing session…`, `… you interrupted`, `— call ended —`), `MANUAL TURN · PRESS SEND`, `SESSION/VIA/PERSONA` tags, failover strip copy, `LIVE TRANSCRIPT · N TURNS`, `YOU`, tools popover, every `aria-label` |
| Providers | column heads, provider `note` prose, all `Spec` labels/values, `LM MODEL`, `AUTO-FAILOVER ON` |
| Settings | section rules (`AUDIO IN/OUT`, `BEHAVIOUR`, `TOOLS`), field labels + hints, switch `OFF/ON`, tool labels |
| Persona card foot | `p.voice` (`Mezzo · 220–340 Hz`), `FIRST MESSAGE`, `JA AGENT` |

**3. The mock transcript is EN-only.** `TRANSCRIPT_SCRIPT` and the caption placeholders don't flip, so in JA mode the call screen shows a Japanese persona speaking English. It needs a JA script (the real app gets JA transcripts from the agent for free, but the mock is what the design is judged on).

**4. Typography is per-element, not per-app.** JA text is opted in with `pp-ja` classes on individual spans. For a whole-app switch the root should carry `data-lang="ja"` and CSS should cascade from there — and three brutalist conventions break in Japanese:
- **ALL-CAPS tracked labels** (`text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.12–0.2em` at 9–10px): uppercase is a no-op, wide tracking fragments kana, and 9px kana is illegible. JA needs ~0.04–0.06em tracking and a 10.5–11px floor.
- **Italic Newsreader** for captions/transcript/desc: italic Japanese is wrong; JA should use Shippori Mincho upright with `line-height ≥ 1.8`.
- **IBM Plex Mono has no CJK glyphs**, so JA in mono contexts falls to whatever the OS picks. Root-level `[data-lang=ja]` font stacks (Zen Kaku Gothic New for UI, Shippori Mincho for display) fix all three in one place and let the per-span `pp-ja` classes go away.

**5. `<html lang="en">` never changes.** It should follow the switch (font fallback, hyphenation, screen-reader voice). In the app that's `document.documentElement.lang`.

**6. Failover direction still symmetric.** Both shells' `useEffect` watches `[lang, provider]` and always reroutes the *provider*. That contradicts what we settled: JA armed on a non-JA transport → reroute to ElevenLabs; non-JA transport *selected* while JA is armed → language drops back to EN with a notice. The prototype needs the two handlers, not one effect — otherwise the design will show a behaviour the app won't have.

**7. Small things:** `LangSwitch` labels `EN / 日本語` are fine, but in JA mode the *other* option should read in the current UI language (`英語 / 日本語`); the sidebar foot `ARIA · 日本語` should show the resolved name `アリア`; the `LANGUAGE` spec's `EN · JA` value and `NO JA AGENT` warnings are engineering-speak that should localize too.

## Recommendation

Do items 1, 2, 4 and 6 in the prototype first (string layer + root `data-lang` + directional failover) — they define the architecture the app will mirror; 3, 5 and 7 fall out of them. On the app side that maps to: `lib/i18n.ts` + a `lang` in app-shell state, `Persona.ja` data in `lib/data.ts`, next/font for the two JA families with `.tsubaki[data-lang=ja]` rules in `globals.css`, `document.documentElement.lang`, and the two selection handlers feeding `resolveElevenLabsAgentId(personaId, lang)`.

Want me to make those changes in the prototype (via DesignSync) so the spec is complete before porting, or start directly on the app?
